finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST to import.php with a `feed` field makes the server fetch an attacker-chosen URL via file_get_contents, enabling blind SSRF (internal hosts, cloud metadata) and local file reads reported only by length.

trace.note: session_start(); no authentication enforced for this branch
file_get_contents() fetches attacker-supplied URL/scheme from the server
Response body discarded; only strlen() echoed, so the attack is blind

finding.guards_checked: No auth (require_admin at lines 4-9 applies only to set_webhook branch). No scheme allowlist. No host/IP blocking (loopback, RFC1918, link-local, metadata). Redirects followed by default in PHP http wrapper, not validated per hop. No DNS pinning. Caveat: http(s)/ftp require allow_url_fopen (PHP default On), not verifiable from code; file:// does not depend on it.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only guard on the sink path is the POST-and-isset check at import.php:11, which does not validate the value. require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is called only in the set_webhook branch (import.php:18), so it does not cover the feed branch. No scheme, host, or IP check exists anywhere in the file.
verdict.reason: $_POST['feed'] at import.php:11 reaches file_get_contents() at import.php:12 with no authentication and no validation, and the response is only echoed as strlen() at import.php:13, so the candidate's trace and blind-SSRF/length-oracle description are accurate. The allow_url_fopen caveat does not affect file:// reads, which PHP supports regardless of that setting.
